A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fisheye3R and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and supplementary material. Relocated and renumbered content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments with VGGT, π3, and MapAnything, along with ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative evaluations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds projection-generalization measurements in Table 2 and mixed-camera driving reconstructions in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Calibration-token insertion, the frozen backbone, three learning schemes, camera-type classification, and attention masks are retained. Both appendices describe the same PyTorch masking implementation; notation changes and removal of an equation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds rendered fisheye evaluation under seven projection settings on Stanford2D3DS, previously used for panoramic evaluation, and a KITTI360 scenario combining front-facing perspective and side-facing fisheye cameras. Existing datasets and reconstruction tasks remain.

E2.justification: The VGGT, π3, MapAnything, and LoRA comparisons retain their comparator membership, including LoRA ranks 4, 8, 16, and 32. The new projection experiment extends evaluation of the existing π3 baseline; newly cited methods are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a controlled evaluation rendering the same Stanford2D3DS source under different projection models and measuring π3 reconstruction with Chamfer distance. Retained experiments keep their stated training budgets, metrics, and model settings. Omitted sampling counts do not establish changed sampling.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a focused robustness test of transfer from Kannala-Brandt synthesis to out-of-distribution parameters and other projections. Figure 6 adds a heterogeneous-camera driving case study. Existing token-count, layer, mixed-input, feature-alignment, and LoRA analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerical projection-generalization results: for example, Table 2 reports MEI Chamfer distance of 0.264 for π3 and 0.095 with adaptation. Figure 6 adds qualitative driving results. The retained benchmark, layer/LoRA-ablation, and efficiency tables have unchanged numerical values.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Equation (16), which explicitly defines masked attention using post-softmax multiplication by the binary mask. The mask construction in Equation (15), learning objectives, and projection equations remain, with other mathematical edits limited to notation and renumbering.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the core claims of lightweight fisheye adaptation across three foundation models, preservation of perspective performance, heterogeneous-camera support, and flexible supervision. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new tests as transfer beyond Kannala-Brandt projections and explains how a front-facing perspective camera connects side-fisheye views. It removes the appendix discussion of resource barriers to training from scratch or full finetuning. The principal architecture and supervision limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address and relabels ADT from synthetic to real in the dataset summary. It removes v1's evaluation counts of 10/1/100 sequences per scene and totals of 300/236/300 for ScanNet++/ADT/KITTI360. Most implementation details and hardware specifications remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gangopadhyay and Wong's perspective-to-fisheye depth/segmentation work and explicitly credits AugUndo as inspiration for the self-supervised objective. It removes the MUST3R citation and associated discussion. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes copyedits throughout, shortens explanations, updates the Google affiliation, and adds acknowledgments. It consolidates appendix Sections 7–9 into Further Discussions and moves the panoramic-generalization discussion into the main results, while retaining the overall narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds the projection-results table and mixed-camera driving figure, moves the existing panoramic Figure 9 into the main text, and rearranges several displays and captions. All earlier figure imagery is retained; the remaining changes largely concern placement and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The controlled projection tests and practical mixed-camera example provide useful additional support for generalization and applicability. Clearer attribution and the code-access pointer also help. These gains are limited by incomplete documentation of the new projection settings and removal of existing evaluation sample counts, but the retained empirical evidence remains intact.
